title: Avoiding interest
hookLine: steps away from interest where possible
tomorrow: what does generosity at work look like when it isn't money?

cards: An envelope in the mail: pre-approved, your name pressed into the card in gold, the low rate in big letters and the later rate in small ones. It's an easy thing to sign.
The Qur'an speaks to the moment, in Pickthall's words: "Allah permitteth trading and forbiddeth usury." The word is riba: interest, the increase charged on a loan.

teach.b: Some people in that time said trade and usury are the same thing. The verse answers them: one is permitted, one is not.
And a little later the Qur'an tells lenders to take back their principal, with no increase: "Wrong not, and ye shall not be wronged." Now the step that makes it human.

In his farewell sermon, reported in Sahih Muslim, the Prophet ﷺ announced that the riba of the old days was abolished, and that the first riba he abolished was his own family's, owed to his uncle al-'Abbas.

teach.h: HE STARTED WITH HIS OWN FAMILY.
teach.b: He started at home. Today, Muslims live among mortgages, student loans and cards, and scholars differ on what real need allows where no interest-free option exists.
What the tradition asks of everyone is direction: no new interest where it can be avoided, the old paid down, better options looked for.
One to tell a friend: the Prophet canceled his own uncle's interest first.

how: Many Muslims look for interest-free banking, home financing and savings, pay down interest debts where they can, and ask scholars about what is allowed when no interest-free option exists.

o: refusing ever to borrow or lend any money
keeping all of your savings as cash at home
stepping away from paying or earning interest

games.q: what the verses and the sermon say — tap the pairs.

s: the Qur'an says trade and usury are the same thing
some said they were alike; 2:275 answers them: trading permitted, usury forbidden.
in his farewell sermon, the Prophet canceled his own uncle's interest first
Sahih Muslim: the first riba abolished was that of al-'Abbas.
Muslim scholars agree on every modern loan
they differ on what real need allows where no interest-free option exists.

games.q: your uncle wants the whole family to drop interest, but his own business still has an interest loan. where does the farewell sermon suggest he start?
o: with everyone else first; the family needs the lesson most.
with his own loan, the way the Prophet began with his own family's.
nowhere yet; he can't speak of it until every debt is gone.
games.why: the Prophet abolished the riba owed to his own uncle first. the step starts at home, even before it's finished.

practice: Close your eyes and bring to mind one place in your money where interest is paid or earned: a card, a loan, a savings account. Name one small step away from it that's actually possible, even if it's only finding out the rate.
Rest with that one step for the rest of the sit.

wordCard.voice: Avoiding interest: stepping away from riba, paying or charging an increase on a loan, as far as you can, starting where you stand.

orig.note: Arabic: usury, the increase charged on a loan, forbidden in Qur'an 2:275.

carryVoice: Here's the line: step by step, away from interest, starting at home the way he did. The shop keeps going.
